name: Daily Pull — daily episode (front-end for the YakYak engine)

parameters.content:
## 📄 YakYak Description — workflow summary (not a step note)
Every day at UTC 06:00 three tarot cards are drawn in a seeded past, present and future spread. The reading is dramatized and rendered as a candle-lit art-nouveau scene.

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: 06:00 UTC daily — CADENCE=daily in show/DailyPull/show.env. Use 'Test workflow' to fire a run by hand (note: manual runs don't extend the no-repeat window).

nodes.name: Show config
nodes.notes: ALL per-show config lives here, on the canvas — the workflow reads no environment variables. Required: campaignId (a campaign the API credential's account owns) and userId (for the balance check). Optional: soundtrackAudioPath (empty = skip the pin), chatWebhookUrl (empty = no announcement). corpusUrl defaults to the cookbook corpus on GitHub — point it at your fork to edit the corpus.

nodes.name: Fetch user
nodes.notes: Same 'YakYak API' Bearer credential as the engine — no token on the canvas or in env. onError=continue so Balance guard can report a clear error instead of a bare 404.

nodes.name: Fetch corpus
nodes.notes: The 22 Major Arcana corpus, fetched from the cookbook repo. No corpus = no episode, so this node fails hard.

nodes.name: Draw cards
nodes.notes: The Randomized (seeded) archetype: same UTC date -> same 3-card draw. The seed, exclusions and draw are all on this node's output — the audit marker.

parameters.jsCode:
const TPL = "You are the head writer for "Daily Pull", a short-form daily tarot series. Each
episode is ONE three-card reading — Past, Present, Future — drawn from the 22 Major
Arcana. The Reader, a warm mystic host, lays the cards and reads them; each drawn
card appears as its own personified figure speaking a single line in its scene.

TODAY'S DRAW ({{DATE}}) — use these EXACT cards and orientations, in this order:
{{BRIEFS}}

CAST — only these four may speak; each scene's leading character must be one of them,
named EXACTLY as written:
  - "The Reader" — the mystic host. Leads Scene 1 (shuffles, names the day's energy and
    the spread) and Scene 5 (synthesises the three cards into one piece of guidance — the
    screenshot caption beat). Warm, grounded, a little uncanny; never doom-mongering.
  - "{{PAST}}" — the PAST card, personified. Leads Scene 2.
  - "{{PRESENT}}" — the PRESENT card, personified. Leads Scene 3.
  - "{{FUTURE}}" — the FUTURE card, personified. Leads Scene 4.

TONE: Intimate, candle-lit, ASMR-calm and a touch mystical. Honest about shadow cards
(Death, The Tower, The Devil) as TRANSFORMATION, never as literal doom or fear-mongering.
General guidance for an anonymous viewer ("you"), never medical, legal or financial advice.

STRUCTURE — exactly 5 scenes:
  1. The Reader — cold open: a candle, the shuffle, naming today's Past/Present/Future spread.
  2. {{PAST}} (Past) — the card reveal and what it says about what shaped you.
  3. {{PRESENT}} (Present) — the card reveal and what it says about right now.
  4. {{FUTURE}} (Future) — the card reveal and where the current is carrying you.
  5. The Reader — closes by weaving the three into one clear takeaway (the caption card).

PER-SCENE REQUIREMENTS:
  - ~180 words of prose briefing the visuals like a director: the card laid on dark velvet,
    candle-light, the personified figure (use the "Figure:" description), the art-nouveau
    ornament. Per-card accent colour can tint the glow.
  - Exactly ONE spoken dialog line per scene, 8–14 words, attributed to the leading character.
    Make it land. Do NOT end the dialog line with a period ("!" or "?" are fine).
  - Only the four cast above may speak.

OUTPUT — reply with ONLY the markdown document below — no preamble, no
triple-backtick fences, nothing after it:

  # Daily Pull — {{DATE}}
  **Generated (UTC):** {{TS}}
  **Spread:** Past · Present · Future (Major Arcana)
  **Draw:** {{DRAW}}

  ## Social title: <punchy title for social posting, 50 characters MAX>

  ## Headlines we drew from:
  - 🔮 Daily Pull — {{DATE}}: {{DRAW}}

  ## Scene 1 — <short title>
  **Leading character:** The Reader
  **Dialog:** "<8–14 word line>"

  <~180 words of scene prose>

  ... (Scene 2 = {{PAST}}, Scene 3 = {{PRESENT}}, Scene 4 = {{FUTURE}}, Scene 5 = The Reader) ...";

// The Daily Pull head-writer prompt, adapted from show/DailyPull/compute.js.
// One change vs the showrunner original: the file-write OUTPUT step becomes
// "reply with only the markdown", plus a requested '## Social title:' line so
// ONE model call covers both the story and the ≤50-char social title.
const ts = new Date().toISOString();
const p = $json;
const fmt = (d) => d.name + (d.isReversed ? ' (reversed)' : '');
const cardBrief = (d) =>
  '  ' + d.position + ' — ' + d.name + (d.isReversed ? ' (REVERSED)' : ' (upright)') + '
' +
  '    Keywords: ' + d.keywords + '
' +
  '    Meaning (' + (d.isReversed ? 'reversed' : 'upright') + '): ' + (d.isReversed ? d.reversedMeaning : d.upright) + '
' +
  '    Figure: ' + d.persona;
const fill = (t, map) => t.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (m, k) => (map[k] === undefined ? m : map[k]));
const prompt = fill(TPL, {
  TS: ts,
  DATE: p.dateStr,
  BRIEFS: p.drawn.map(cardBrief).join('
'),
  PAST: p.drawn[0].name,
  PRESENT: p.drawn[1].name,
  FUTURE: p.drawn[2].name,
  DRAW: p.drawn.map((d) => d.position + ' — ' + fmt(d)).join(' · '),
});
return [{ json: { prompt } }];

nodes.name: Write story (Claude)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'claude-opus-4-8', max_tokens: 16000, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, messages: [ { role: 'user', content: $json.prompt } ] } }}

nodes.notes: Messages API over raw HTTP (no SDK inside n8n). Auth via the 'Anthropic API key' Header Auth credential (header name x-api-key). Adaptive thinking; the story lands in the response's text block.

nodes.name: Build story payload
nodes.notes: The story markdown is preserved on this node's output — n8n's execution log is the story archive (the showrunner's stories/ equivalent).

nodes.name: Call engine

workflowId.cachedResultName: YakYak engine — resolve target, patch or new episode, render, post

nodes.notes: Fires the generic YakYak engine in episode mode. The engine only responds once the episode is generated AND rendered. Retry is safe: a re-run lands on the same unrendered slot. Announcement happens here (below), not in the engine.

nodes.name: Set social fields

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ Object.assign({ movieId: $json.movieId }, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle ? { socialTitle: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle } : {}, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption ? { socialDescription: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption } : {}) }}

nodes.notes: Showrunner parity: ≤50-char social title + caption. onError=continue — cosmetic metadata must not kill a rendered episode.

nodes.name: Announce

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { text: '🔮 Daily Pull episode ready — "' + ($('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle || 'Daily reading') + '": ' + $('Call engine').first().json.url } }}

nodes.notes: Review-first output event (the safe default). chatWebhookUrl empty → this node errors and the run still succeeds (onError=continue). Auto-posting to social is the deliberate next step — see the BBN guide §4.3.
